You will solve quadratic equations by taking square roots and by using the quadratic formula from the GED formula sheet, rounding when needed.
You will find the vertex, axis of symmetry, intercepts, and maximum or minimum of a parabola from its equation or graph, and use them in word problems.

Quadratics and Functions; Full Math Review

  • Solve quadratic equations by factoring

  • Review the whole GED math test and plan for test day

Today: warm-up, factoring, square roots and the formula, parabolas, linear vs. quadratic, mixed review, test-day strategy

notes.say: Welcome to the final week of math. Quadratics are the last big algebra topic on the GED, and they use tools you already own: factoring from Week 7, solving equations from Week 8, and graphing from Week 9. The first two-thirds of today is new teaching on quadratics. The last third pulls the whole course together so you walk into the test knowing what is on it and how you will attack it. Same rhythm as always: I explain, I show a worked example, we do some together, and then you try some on your own while I watch the clock.
ask: Which earlier math topic do you feel best about, and which one still worries you? (expected answer: any; note the weak topic and lean on it during the review slides 22–25)
notes.watch: Pacing for 60 minutes: warm-up 5 min (slide 2); factoring 11 min (slides 3–7); square roots and the formula 12 min (slides 8–13); parabolas 11 min (slides 14–18); linear vs. quadratic 6 min (slides 19–21); full review 11 min (slides 22–25); strategy and recap 4 min (slides 26–27). If you fall behind, cut the third problem on each we-do slide and keep the review slides.

slides.title: Warm-up: Lines and Functions (Week 9 Review)
slides.board:
Work these on paper. No calculator.

  1. Find the slope of the line through (1, 2) and (4, 11).
  2. What is the y-intercept of y = −2x + 7?
  3. If f(x) = x2 − 3x, find f(−2).
  4. Write the equation of the line with slope 4 and y-intercept −3.
  5. Is the relation {(1, 2), (2, 5), (1, 7)} a function? Why or why not?
steps: 2. In y = mx + b, b is the y-intercept: 7, the point (0, 7)
4. y = mx + b with m = 4 and b = −3: y = 4x − 3
5. No. The input 1 is paired with two outputs (2 and 7), so it is not a function.

notes.say: These are last week's skills, and every one of them comes back today. Slope and intercepts come back when we compare lines with parabolas, and function notation comes back every time we find a vertex. Take about three minutes, then read me your answers one at a time.
ask: On number 3, what do you get for (−2)<sup>2</sup>, and why? (expected answer: 4, because a negative times a negative is positive)
On number 5, which x-value causes the problem? (expected answer: x = 1 is paired with two different y-values)
notes.answer: (1) (11 − 2)/(4 − 1) = 9/3 = 3   (2) 7, the point (0, 7)   (3) (−2)<sup>2</sup> − 3(−2) = 4 + 6 = 10   (4) y = 4x − 3   (5) No; the input 1 has two outputs, 2 and 7.
notes.watch: Number 3 is the warm-up that matters most for today. If the student gets −2 (from writing −4 + 6) or −10, they squared the 2 and then attached the sign. Fix it now: put the negative number in parentheses, (−2)<sup>2</sup> = 4. That same habit prevents sign errors in the quadratic formula later.

slides.title: Quadratic Equations and the Zero Product Property
slides.board:
• A quadratic equation has x2 as its highest power.
  • Standard form: ax2 + bx + c = 0, with a ≠ 0. The sign belongs to the number: in 2x2 − 7x + 3 = 0, a = 2, b = −7, c = 3.
  • Expect two solutions (also called roots or zeros).
  • Zero product property: if A × B = 0, then A = 0 or B = 0. It works only with 0.

Solve by factoring: (1) get 0 on one side   (2) factor   (3) set each factor = 0   (4) solve and check

notes.say: A quadratic is any equation where the highest power of x is 2. The reason we can solve them by factoring is one simple fact: the only way two numbers can multiply to zero is if one of them is zero. So if I can rewrite the equation as "something times something equals zero," I can split it into two small equations I already know how to solve. That is why the very first step is always to get zero alone on one side. The zero product property works only with zero. If two numbers multiply to 6, they could be 2 and 3, or 1 and 6, or a hundred other pairs, so we learn nothing.
ask: In 4x<sup>2</sup> − x − 9 = 0, what are a, b, and c? (expected answer: a = 4, b = −1, c = −9)
Quick factoring check from Week 7: factor x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 6. (expected answer: (x + 2)(x + 3))
If (x − 3)(x + 5) = 0, what are the solutions? (expected answer: x = 3 or x = −5)
notes.watch: Students often read b as 1 in 4x<sup>2</sup> − x − 9 because no number is written. A lone x means 1x, and the minus sign comes with it, so b = −1. Also listen for "x = −3 or x = 5" on the last question: the solution has the opposite sign of the number inside the factor.

slides.title: Solve by Factoring
slides.board:
Solve: x2 − 5x − 14 = 0

Method: find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b. Then use the zero product property.
steps: It already equals 0. Find two numbers with product −14 and sum −5.
Pairs for −14: 1 and −14, −1 and 14, 2 and −7, −2 and 7. Only 2 + (−7) = −5.
x + 2 = 0 gives x = −2.   x − 7 = 0 gives x = 7.

notes.say: This equation already has zero on one side, so we go straight to factoring. I need two numbers that multiply to negative 14 and add to negative 5. Because the product is negative, one number is positive and one is negative. Because the sum is negative, the negative one is bigger. Once it is factored, each factor gets its own tiny equation. Then we check both answers in the original equation, which takes ten seconds and catches sign slips.
ask: Why must one of the two numbers be negative? (expected answer: their product, −14, is negative)
notes.watch: The most common slip is (x − 2)(x + 7), which multiplies back to x<sup>2</sup> + 5x − 14, the wrong middle sign. Have the student multiply the factors back out whenever they are unsure.

slides.title: Get Zero First, and Never Divide by x
slides.board:
Solve each equation.

(a) 3x2 = 12x

(b) x(x + 3) = 10

Neither one equals 0 yet. Move everything to one side first.
steps: (a) Factor out the GCF, 3x: 3x(x − 4) = 0, so 3x = 0 or x − 4 = 0: x = 0 or x = 4

notes.say: These two equations set the two classic traps. In part (a), many people divide both sides by x and get only x = 4. That throws away the answer x = 0, because dividing by x quietly assumes x is not zero. Factor out the x instead. In part (b), the left side is already factored, so it is tempting to set x = 10 and x + 3 = 10. That is wrong, because the product is 10, not 0. Multiply it out, subtract 10, and then factor.
ask: In part (b), why can we not set each factor equal to 10? (expected answer: the zero product property only works when the product is 0)
notes.watch: If the student answers "x = 4" only for part (a), ask: "Does x = 0 work? 3(0)<sup>2</sup> = 12(0)?" It does, so it must be a solution. If they answer "x = 10 or x = 7" for part (b), check x = 10: 10 × 13 = 130, not 10.

slides.title: Factoring Together
slides.board:
Tell me the first step before you solve.

  1. x2 + 7x + 12 = 0
  2. x2 − 49 = 0
  3. 5x2 − 20x = 0
  4. x2 − x = 12
steps: 1. Product 12, sum 7: 3 and 4. (x + 3)(x + 4) = 0, so x = −3 or x = −4
2. Difference of squares: (x + 7)(x − 7) = 0, so x = −7 or x = 7
4. Subtract 12: x2 − x − 12 = 0. Product −12, sum −1: −4 and 3. (x − 4)(x + 3) = 0, so x = 4 or x = −3

notes.say: Let's do these together. For each one, tell me what kind of factoring it needs before you tell me the answers: a trinomial, a difference of two squares, or a greatest common factor. And on number 4, tell me what has to happen before any factoring at all.
ask: Which problem is a difference of two squares? (expected answer: number 2, x<sup>2</sup> − 49 = (x + 7)(x − 7))
What is the first step on number 4? (expected answer: subtract 12 so the equation equals 0)
notes.answer: (1) (x + 3)(x + 4) = 0, so x = −3 or x = −4   (2) (x + 7)(x − 7) = 0, so x = 7 or x = −7   (3) 5x(x − 4) = 0, so x = 0 or x = 4   (4) x<sup>2</sup> − x − 12 = 0, (x − 4)(x + 3) = 0, so x = 4 or x = −3
notes.watch: On number 1, positive answers (3 and 4) mean the student copied the numbers from the factors without solving. On number 2, an answer of only 7 means the negative root was lost. On number 3, an answer of only 4 means the student divided by x.

slides.title: Your Turn: Solve by Factoring
slides.board:
Three minutes. Find both solutions of each equation.

  1. x2 − 9x + 20 = 0
  2. x2 + 2x − 24 = 0
  3. 2x2 = 18x

notes.say: Your turn. I am starting the clock for three minutes. Write every step: zero on one side, the factored form, then the two small equations. When time is up, read me both solutions for each problem.
ask: Read me both solutions for each problem. (expected answer: 4 and 5; −6 and 4; 0 and 9)
notes.answer: (1) (x − 4)(x − 5) = 0, so x = 4 or x = 5   (2) (x + 6)(x − 4) = 0, so x = −6 or x = 4   (3) 2x<sup>2</sup> − 18x = 0, 2x(x − 9) = 0, so x = 0 or x = 9
notes.watch: If number 3 comes back as "9" only, the student divided by x; send them back to slide 5. If number 2 comes back as 6 and −4, the signs in the factors were swapped: multiply (x − 6)(x + 4) back out to show it gives −2x, not +2x.

slides.title: Square Roots and the Quadratic Formula
slides.board:
No x term? Get x2 alone, then take ± the square root: x2 = 49 → x = ±7.

Will not factor? Use the quadratic formula. It is on the GED formula sheet:

x = (−b ± √(b2 − 4ac)) / (2a)

  • Write a, b, and c with their signs. Put negatives in parentheses.
  • Find b2 − 4ac (the discriminant) first.
  • Divide the whole top by 2a.

notes.say: Factoring is fast when it works, but many quadratics on the GED will not factor with whole numbers. Two other tools handle everything else. If there is no x term, just isolate x squared and take the square root, and always write plus or minus, because both 7 and negative 7 square to 49. The quadratic formula works on every quadratic equation, and the GED gives it to you on the formula sheet. The danger is not remembering it; the danger is signs. So we label a, b, and c first, compute the part under the square root by itself, and only then build the two answers. That number under the square root, b squared minus 4ac, is called the discriminant. If it is positive there are two solutions, if it is zero there is one, and if it is negative there are no real solutions.
ask: In x<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 3 = 0, what is −b? (expected answer: 4, the opposite of −4)
What is (−4)<sup>2</sup>? (expected answer: 16, not −16)
notes.watch: Two errors cause most wrong answers: writing −b as −4 when b is already −4, and dividing only the square root by 2a instead of the whole top. Insist on parentheses for every substituted value and a fraction bar under the entire numerator.

slides.title: Solving by Square Roots
slides.board:
Solve each equation.

(a) 3x2 − 75 = 0

(b) (x − 2)2 = 16
steps: (a) Take ± the square root: x = 5 or x = −5
(b) Take ± the square root of both sides: x − 2 = 4 or x − 2 = −4

notes.say: When there is no plain x term, factoring is extra work. Undo the operations around x squared the same way you would solve any equation, then take the square root of both sides. Part (b) looks harder but is the same idea: the whole quantity x minus 2 is being squared, so its square root is plus or minus 4. That gives two small linear equations.
ask: In part (b), what two numbers could x − 2 equal? (expected answer: 4 and −4)
notes.watch: The most common mistake is writing only the positive root. In part (b), a student who writes only x − 2 = 4 gets x = 6 and misses x = −2. Ask: "What else squares to 16?"

slides.title: The Quadratic Formula, Step by Step
slides.board:
Solve: 2x2 + 3x − 5 = 0

x = (−b ± √(b2 − 4ac)) / (2a)

notes.say: Here is the formula with every step written out. First I label a, b, and c, and I circle the negative on c. Then I compute the discriminant by itself, take its square root, and finally split into a plus answer and a minus answer. Because the discriminant came out to a perfect square, 49, the answers are exact numbers with no rounding. That is a sign the equation could also have been factored.
ask: What is 4ac here, and is it positive or negative? (expected answer: 4(2)(−5) = −40, so subtracting it adds 40)
notes.watch: Watch for 9 − 40 = −31 under the square root: the student dropped the sign of c. Minus a negative is plus: 9 − (−40) = 49.

slides.title: The Quadratic Formula Together
slides.board:
Label a, b, and c first. Round to the nearest hundredth when needed.

  1. x2 − 4x − 3 = 0
  2. 3x2 − x − 2 = 0
  3. x2 + 6x + 2 = 0
steps: 1. a = 1, b = −4, c = −3. Discriminant: 16 + 12 = 28. x = (4 ± 5.2915)/2: x ≈ 4.65 or x ≈ −0.65
2. a = 3, b = −1, c = −2. Discriminant: 1 + 24 = 25. x = (1 ± 5)/6: x = 1 or x = −2/3
3. a = 1, b = 6, c = 2. Discriminant: 36 − 8 = 28. x = (−6 ± 5.2915)/2: x ≈ −0.35 or x ≈ −5.65

notes.say: Now you run the formula and I will keep you honest on the signs. Tell me a, b, and c out loud before anything else. On the calculator, find the square root of the discriminant and write it down to four decimal places before you add or subtract, then round only at the very end.
ask: On number 1, what is the discriminant? (expected answer: (−4)<sup>2</sup> − 4(1)(−3) = 16 + 12 = 28)
On number 2, is the discriminant a perfect square? What does that tell you? (expected answer: yes, 25; the answers are exact)
notes.answer: (1) x = (4 ± √28)/2 ≈ 4.65 or −0.65   (2) x = (1 ± 5)/6, so x = 1 or x = −2/3   (3) x = (−6 ± √28)/2 ≈ −0.35 or −5.65
notes.watch: On number 1, answers near 0.65 and −4.65 mean the student used −4 for −b. On number 2, answers of 2 and −4/3 mean the student divided by a (3) instead of 2a (6).

slides.title: GED-Style Question: The Quadratic Formula
slides.board:
What are the solutions of the equation below, rounded to the nearest hundredth?

x2 − 6x + 4 = 0

A. x ≈ 10.47 and x ≈ 1.53    B. x ≈ −0.76 and x ≈ −5.24
C. x ≈ 5.24 and x ≈ 0.76    D. x ≈ 6.61 and x ≈ −0.61
steps: Eliminate B: it comes from using −6 for −b. Since b = −6, −b = +6: (6 ± 4.47)/2, not (−6 ± 4.47)/2.
Eliminate D: it comes from adding 4ac: 36 + 16 = 52. The formula subtracts: 36 − 4(1)(4) = 36 − 16 = 20.
Eliminate A: it comes from forgetting to divide by 2a = 2: 6 ± 4.47 gives 10.47 and 1.53.
C is correct: discriminant 20, √20 ≈ 4.4721, x = (6 + 4.4721)/2 ≈ 5.24 and x = (6 − 4.4721)/2 ≈ 0.76. Check: 5.242 − 6(5.24) + 4 ≈ 0.

notes.say: Every wrong choice here is the answer you get from one specific slip in the formula, so landing on one of the choices proves nothing. Work it, then use the other choices as a checklist of the traps you avoided. There is also a fast check: substitute your answer back in. For x = 5.24, x squared minus 6x plus 4 should come out very close to zero.
ask: Which choice did you get, and what was your discriminant? (expected answer: C; the discriminant is 36 − 16 = 20)
notes.answer: C. a = 1, b = −6, c = 4. b<sup>2</sup> − 4ac = 36 − 16 = 20; √20 ≈ 4.4721. x = (6 ± 4.4721)/2 ≈ 5.24 or 0.76.
notes.watch: If the student picked B, D, or A, read the matching elimination step aloud and have them find the exact line where their work changed.

slides.title: Your Turn: Choose a Method
slides.board:
Three minutes. Pick the fastest method for each: square roots, factoring, or the formula.

  1. x2 = 81
  2. x2 + 4x − 21 = 0
  3. x2 + 2x − 5 = 0 (nearest hundredth)

notes.say: Part of being fast on the GED is choosing the right tool. Before you solve each one, write the method next to it. If there is no x term, use square roots. If you can find the two numbers quickly, factor. If you cannot find them in about twenty seconds, go straight to the formula.
ask: Which method did you choose for each, and what did you get? (expected answer: square roots, ±9; factoring, −7 and 3; formula, about 1.45 and −3.45)
notes.answer: (1) x = ±9   (2) (x + 7)(x − 3) = 0, so x = −7 or x = 3   (3) discriminant 4 + 20 = 24, √24 ≈ 4.899, x = (−2 ± 4.899)/2 ≈ 1.45 or −3.45
notes.watch: If number 3 comes back as 3.45 and −1.45, the student used +2 for −b. If they tried to factor number 3 for a long time, point out that no pair of whole numbers multiplies to −5 and adds to 2 (only 5 and −1, or −5 and 1), so the formula is the right call.

slides.title: Graphs of Quadratics: Parabolas
slides.board:
• The graph of y = ax2 + bx + c is a U-shaped parabola.
  • a > 0: opens up, lowest point (minimum). a < 0: opens down, highest point (maximum).
  • Vertex (turning point): x = −b/(2a), then substitute to find y. Not on the formula sheet.
  • Axis of symmetry: the vertical line through the vertex.
  • y-intercept: (0, c).   x-intercepts: solve ax2 + bx + c = 0.

The graph shows y = x2 (opens up) and y = −x2 + 4 (opens down).

notes.say: Every quadratic function draws the same basic shape, a parabola. The sign of a tells you which way it opens: positive a is a smile with a lowest point, negative a is a frown with a highest point. The turning point is the vertex. Its x-coordinate comes from negative b over 2a. Memorize that one, because the formula sheet gives you the quadratic formula but not the vertex formula. Notice it is just the front part of the quadratic formula. Finally, connect this to the first half of today: the x-intercepts are exactly the solutions of the equation, because on the x-axis y equals zero. Solving a quadratic and finding where its graph crosses the x-axis are the same job.
ask: Does y = −2x<sup>2</sup> + 3 open up or down? Does it have a maximum or a minimum? (expected answer: down, so a maximum)
Where does y = x<sup>2</sup> − 4x + 7 cross the y-axis? (expected answer: (0, 7))
notes.watch: Students mix up the intercepts. An x-intercept has y = 0, so it is written (x, 0); the y-intercept has x = 0, written (0, y). Point to the graph: the x-intercepts sit on the horizontal axis.

slides.title: Key Features of a Parabola
slides.board:
For y = x2 − 6x + 5, find:

  • which way it opens
  • the y-intercept
  • the x-intercepts
  • the vertex and the axis of symmetry
steps: a = 1 is positive, so it opens up and the vertex is a minimum.
y-intercept: set x = 0, y = 5. The point is (0, 5).
Vertex: x = −(−6)/(2 × 1) = 6/2 = 3. y = 32 − 6(3) + 5 = 9 − 18 + 5 = −4. Vertex (3, −4); axis of symmetry x = 3.
Check: 3 is halfway between 1 and 5. The minimum value of y is −4.

notes.say: Here is the full routine on one parabola. I will do the easy features first, the direction and the y-intercept, which take five seconds each. Then the x-intercepts by factoring, and finally the vertex with negative b over 2a. Look at how the answers agree with each other on the graph: the vertex sits exactly halfway between the two x-intercepts. That gives you a free check.
ask: Halfway between x = 1 and x = 5 is what number? (expected answer: 3, the x-coordinate of the vertex)
notes.watch: If the student gets x = −3 for the vertex, they dropped the negative in −b/(2a). Here b = −6, so −b = 6 and x = 6/2 = 3.

slides.title: Maximum Height: A Word Problem
slides.board:
A ball is thrown straight up from the ground. Its height in feet after t seconds is

h = −16t2 + 64t

What is its greatest height, and when does it land?
steps: Greatest height is at the vertex: t = −b/(2a) = −64/(2 × −16) = −64/−32 = 2 seconds.
Lands when h = 0: −16t<sup>2</sup> + 64t = 0 → −16t(t − 4) = 0 → t = 0 or t = 4.
t = 0 is the throw, so it lands after 4 seconds. (The vertex time, 2, is halfway between 0 and 4.)

notes.say: Real GED quadratics are often about things thrown in the air, or about area and profit. The question words tell you which feature to find. "Greatest," "highest," or "maximum" means the vertex. "Hits the ground" or "lands" means the height is zero, so you solve the equation. Here a is negative 16, so the parabola opens down and the vertex really is a maximum. The chart shows the height every half second, and you can see it rise to 64 feet and come back down.
ask: Which feature answers "when does it land"? (expected answer: the x-intercept, where h = 0)
Why is t = 0 not the answer for landing? (expected answer: that is the moment it is thrown)
notes.watch: Students often answer the time of the maximum (2 seconds) when asked for the greatest height. Ask: "Is 2 a height or a time?" Then substitute it to get 64 feet.

slides.title: Parabolas Together
slides.board:
The graph shows y = −x2 + 4x + 5. Find each feature with algebra, then check it on the graph.

  1. Opens up or down? Maximum or minimum?
  2. The vertex
  3. The y-intercept
  4. The x-intercepts
steps: 1. a = −1 is negative: opens down, so the vertex is a maximum.
4. −x2 + 4x + 5 = 0 → x2 − 4x − 5 = 0 → (x − 5)(x + 1) = 0: (5, 0) and (−1, 0). On the graph, both sit on the x-axis, 3 units either side of x = 2.

notes.say: This time you do the algebra and the graph is your answer checker. Tell me each feature, then we will find it on the picture together. When a is negative, I like to multiply the whole equation by negative 1 before factoring; the solutions do not change.
ask: What is −b/(2a) here? (expected answer: −4/(2 × −1) = 2)
Can we multiply −x<sup>2</sup> + 4x + 5 = 0 by −1? Why? (expected answer: yes; multiplying both sides of an equation by the same nonzero number keeps the solutions)
notes.answer: (1) a = −1, so it opens down and has a maximum. (2) x = −4/(−2) = 2; y = −4 + 8 + 5 = 9; vertex (2, 9). (3) (0, 5). (4) x<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 5 = 0 → (x − 5)(x + 1) = 0 → (5, 0) and (−1, 0).
notes.watch: If the student gives the vertex as (−2, …), they lost a sign: −4 divided by −2 is positive 2. Have them confirm on the graph that the top of the curve is to the right of the y-axis.

slides.title: Your Turn: Parabolas
slides.board:
Three minutes.

  1. Find the vertex of y = x2 + 8x + 10.
  2. Find the y-intercept of y = 2x2 − 5x + 7.
  3. Does y = −3x2 + 6x + 1 have a maximum or a minimum? What is that value?
  4. Find the x-intercepts of y = x2 − 2x − 8.

notes.say: Your turn. Use the routine: sign of a, then the y-intercept, then the vertex with negative b over 2a, then the x-intercepts by solving. Write the points as ordered pairs. Read me your four answers when the clock stops.
ask: Read me your four answers as ordered pairs or values. (expected answer: (−4, −6); (0, 7); maximum 4; (4, 0) and (−2, 0))
notes.answer: (1) x = −8/2 = −4; y = 16 − 32 + 10 = −6; vertex (−4, −6)   (2) (0, 7)   (3) a < 0, so a maximum: x = −6/(−6) = 1, y = −3 + 6 + 1 = 4; the maximum is 4   (4) (x − 4)(x + 2) = 0, so (4, 0) and (−2, 0)
notes.watch: On number 3, an answer of 1 is the x-coordinate, not the maximum value. On number 4, (0, 4) and (0, −2) put the values in the wrong position: x-intercepts always have y = 0.

slides.title: Linear or Quadratic? Read the Changes
slides.board:
x01234
Linear: y = 3x + 11471013
Quadratic: y = x2014916
  • Linear: same change every step (+3, +3, +3, +3). Straight line.
  • Quadratic: changes +1, +3, +5, +7; the changes grow by the same amount (+2). Parabola.
  • An upward parabola eventually passes any line. To compare, substitute and compute.

notes.say: On the GED you will see functions as equations, tables, graphs, and word descriptions, and you will be asked which one is greater, which grows faster, or what kind it is. The table test is the fastest. Subtract each output from the next one. If those first differences are all the same, the function is linear. If they are not the same but the differences of the differences are constant, the function is quadratic. Notice that x squared starts below the line, but by x equals 4 it has passed it. That always happens with an upward parabola, which is why you should never guess from the first few values. Compute at the x-value the question asks about.
ask: A table's y-values go 5, 8, 11, 14. Linear or quadratic? (expected answer: linear; it goes up by 3 every time)
Another goes 2, 3, 6, 11, 18. Linear or quadratic? (expected answer: quadratic; changes 1, 3, 5, 7 grow by 2)
notes.watch: Some students call any increasing table "linear." Increasing is not enough; the change has to be the same every step. Make them write the differences under the table.

slides.title: Comparing a Line and a Parabola
slides.board:
f(x) = 5x + 2 and g(x) = x2

  1. Which is greater at x = 3? At x = 6?
  2. Which increases more from x = 3 to x = 5?

The chart shows both functions for x = 0 to 6.
steps: At x = 3: f(3) = 5(3) + 2 = 17 and g(3) = 32 = 9. f is greater.
At x = 6: f(6) = 5(6) + 2 = 32 and g(6) = 62 = 36. g is greater.
From x = 3 to x = 5: f goes 17 → 27, up 10. g goes 9 → 25, up 16.
g increases more on that interval, even though f was ahead at x = 3.

notes.say: Here is the kind of comparison the GED likes. The line starts ahead, and for small x it is clearly bigger. But the parabola is speeding up, and by x equals 6 it has caught and passed the line. Rate of change over an interval is just the change in output. For a line it is the same over any interval of the same width. For the parabola it keeps growing.
ask: Read the chart: about where do the two graphs cross? (expected answer: between x = 5 and x = 6)
notes.watch: If the student says "f is always greater because it starts higher," compute f(6) and g(6) together. The numbers settle it: 32 versus 36.

slides.title: GED-Style Question: Linear or Quadratic?
slides.board:
The table shows values of a function.

x01234
y3471219

Which statement is true?

A. It is linear, because y increases every time x increases.
B. It is linear, with a rate of change of 4.
C. It is quadratic, because the second differences are all 2.
D. It is quadratic, because the first differences are all 2.
steps: Eliminate A: increasing is not enough. A linear function must change by the same amount each step, and this one changes by 1, then 3, then 5, then 7.
Eliminate B: 4 is only the average change from x = 0 to x = 4: (19 − 3)/4. The step-by-step changes are not all 4.
Eliminate D: the first differences are 1, 3, 5, 7, not all 2. It is the second differences that are 2.
C is correct: first differences 1, 3, 5, 7; second differences 2, 2, 2. Constant second differences mean quadratic. (The rule is y = x2 + 3.)

notes.say: Each wrong choice here is a half-true idea. Write the first differences under the table, then the second differences, and the answer is no longer a guess.
ask: What are the first differences? (expected answer: 1, 3, 5, 7)
notes.answer: C. First differences: 1, 3, 5, 7 (not constant). Second differences: 2, 2, 2 (constant), so the function is quadratic.
notes.watch: Choice B is the sneakiest: (19 − 3)/(4 − 0) = 4 is the average rate of change over the whole table, but a linear function needs the same change every step.

Today's review is not about relearning everything. It is about knowing the map so you can spot which skill a question is testing in the first ten seconds. Know what the formula sheet gives you and what it does not. If a formula is on the sheet, you only need to know when to use it. If it is not, like the vertex formula or percent change, it has to be in your head.

Looking at this map, which row has your weakest skill? (expected answer: any; write it down for the study plan)

slides.title: Mixed Review Together

Four skills from four different weeks. Name the skill first.

  2. A right triangle has legs 9 and 12. How long is the hypotenuse?

notes.watch: On number 1, $21.60 alone means the student found the tip but not the total; reread the question. On number 2, 21 means they added the legs. On number 3, x = 9 means they wrote 3x − 4 instead of distributing the 3 to both terms.

slides.title: GED-Style Question: Mixed Review
slides.board:
A cylindrical water tank has a diameter of 6 feet and a height of 10 feet. To the nearest tenth, what is its volume in cubic feet? Use π ≈ 3.14.

A. 188.4    B. 282.6    C. 1,130.4    D. 94.2
steps: Eliminate C: it uses the diameter as the radius: 3.14 × 62 × 10 = 1,130.4.
Eliminate D: it forgets to square the radius: 3.14 × 3 × 10 = 94.2.
Eliminate A: 2 × 3.14 × 3 × 10 = 188.4 is the area of the curved side (part of the surface area), not the volume.
B is correct: r = 3, so V = πr2h = 3.14 × 9 × 10 = 282.6 cubic feet.

notes.say: This is a Week 6 question, and it shows why the formula sheet is a tool and not a crutch. The sheet gives you V = πr<sup>2</sup>h, but it will not remind you that the problem gave a diameter. Every wrong choice here comes from a real slip with r.
ask: What is the radius? (expected answer: 3 feet, half of the diameter)
notes.watch: If the student picked C, they used 6 as the radius. Have them underline "diameter" in the stem and write r = ___ before using any formula.

slides.title: Your Turn: Mixed Review Lightning Round

  2. Solve 2x − 7 > 9.
  3. A standard number cube is rolled once. What is the probability of an even number?
  4. Write 0.00042 in scientific notation.

ask: Read me your answers and the skill for each. (expected answer: 8x<sup>5</sup>, exponents; x > 8, inequalities; 1/2, probability; 4.2 × 10^−4, scientific notation)

slides.title: GED Strategy: Plug In, Check the Sheet, Pace Yourself
slides.board:
1. Plug answers back in. For "which values solve…," substitute each choice. A true solution makes the equation exactly 0.
  2. Use the formula sheet for the quadratic formula, but label a, b, c with signs first.
  3. Calculator: on the TI-30XS, find √(b2 − 4ac) first and write it down; then add and subtract.
  4. Pace: 115 minutes for about 46 questions, roughly 2.5 minutes each. Flag, guess, and come back.
  5. Never leave a blank. A wrong answer costs nothing extra.

notes.say: Quadratics are the one place on the GED where checking an answer can be faster than finding it. If the choices are pairs of numbers, substitute one value from each pair into the equation; the wrong pairs usually fail on the first number. For the formula, the calculator is your friend, but only if you use it in pieces. Find the square root of the discriminant, write it down, and then do the plus and the minus separately. Typing the whole formula in one line is where parentheses get lost. And for the whole test: about two and a half minutes a question. If one is eating your time, flag it, pick your best guess, and move on.

screens.title: What You Will Learn
screens.html:
This is the final week of the course. You will learn the last big algebra topic on the GED math test, quadratics, and then review the whole test. Quadratics use skills you already have: factoring (Week 7), solving equations (Week 8), and graphing (Week 9).

By the end, you will be able to:

  • Solve quadratic equations by factoring, including equations with a greatest common factor.
  • Solve quadratic equations by taking square roots and by using the quadratic formula.
  • Find the vertex, intercepts, and maximum or minimum of a parabola, and use them in word problems.
  • Tell linear and quadratic functions apart and compare them.
  • See the whole GED math test at a glance and know what is on the formula sheet.

Keep paper and a pencil next to you. A calculator helps for the quadratic formula screens.

screens.title: Quadratic Equations and Standard Form
screens.html:
A quadratic equation has x2 as its highest power. Its standard form is

ax2 + bx + c = 0   (a is not 0)

All the terms are on one side and 0 is on the other. The letters a, b, and c are the numbers in front of x2, in front of x, and alone.

  • The sign belongs to the number. In 2x2 − 7x + 3 = 0, a = 2, b = −7, and c = 3.
  • A lone x means 1x. In x2 − x − 6 = 0, a = 1 and b = −1.
  • A missing term means 0. In x2 − 25 = 0, b = 0.

Most quadratic equations have two solutions (also called roots or zeros), so expect two answers.

example.prompt: Write 3x<sup>2</sup> = 5x + 2 in standard form and name a, b, and c.
steps: Move every term to the left side. Subtract 5x and subtract 2 from both sides: 3x<sup>2</sup> − 5x − 2 = 0.
Read the numbers with their signs: a = 3, b = −5, c = −2.

check.prompt:
Write x(x + 3) = 10 in standard form, ax2 + bx + c = 0. Type the expression that goes on the left side of "= 0".

Type x^2 for x squared, like this: x^2 + 5x − 2.

mistakes.why: You multiplied out the left side but left the 10 on the right. Standard form needs 0 alone on the right, so subtract 10: x<sup>2</sup> + 3x − 10.
Moving 10 to the left side means subtracting it, not adding it: x<sup>2</sup> + 3x − 10 = 0.
You multiplied only the first term by x, getting x<sup>2</sup> + 3. Distribute x to both terms: x(x + 3) = x<sup>2</sup> + 3x. Then subtract 10.

check.hint: Multiply out x(x + 3) first. Then subtract 10 from both sides so the right side is 0.
check.explain:
Distribute: x(x + 3) = x2 + 3x, so the equation is x2 + 3x = 10.

Subtract 10 from both sides: x2 + 3x − 10 = 0.

The left side is x2 + 3x − 10, so a = 1, b = 3, and c = −10.

A common mistake is to stop at x2 + 3x. The 10 must move to the left side, where it becomes −10.

screens.title: The Zero Product Property
screens.html:
Solving a quadratic by factoring depends on one fact:

Zero product property: if A × B = 0, then A = 0 or B = 0.

The only way two numbers can multiply to 0 is if at least one of them is 0. So when a quadratic is written as (factor)(factor) = 0, you can split it into two small equations.

This works only with 0. If (x − 2)(x + 1) = 6, you cannot set each factor equal to 6. Many pairs of numbers multiply to 6.

Notice that each solution has the opposite sign of the number inside its factor: the factor x − 4 gives x = 4, and the factor x + 9 gives x = −9.

steps: Set the first factor equal to 0: x − 4 = 0, so x = 4.
Set the second factor equal to 0: x + 9 = 0, so x = −9.

mistakes.why: You copied the number from the factor x − 2. Setting x − 2 = 0 gives x = 2, which is positive. The negative solution comes from x + 7 = 0, so x = −7.
x + 7 = 0 means x = −7, not 7. Subtract 7 from both sides.

check.hint: Set each factor equal to 0 and solve. Then pick the negative answer.
check.explain:
x + 7 = 0 gives x = −7.   x − 2 = 0 gives x = 2.

The negative solution is −7.

If you answered −2, you copied the number inside the factor x − 2 instead of solving x − 2 = 0.

screens.title: Solving by Factoring a Trinomial
screens.html:
When the equation looks like x2 + bx + c = 0, factor it the way you did in Week 7: find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b.

  1. Get 0 on one side.
  2. Factor.
  3. Set each factor equal to 0.
  4. Solve each small equation, then check.

Sign clues: if c is positive, both numbers have the same sign as b. If c is negative, the numbers have opposite signs, and the one with the larger size has the sign of b.

steps: Find two numbers with product −15 and sum 2. Since c is negative, the signs differ: 5 and −3.
x + 5 = 0 gives x = −5. x − 3 = 0 gives x = 3.

mistakes.why: You factored as (x + 3)(x + 8), which gives +11x, not −11x. Both numbers must be negative: (x − 3)(x − 8) = 0, so x = 3 or x = 8.
x = 3 is a solution, but it is the smaller one. The solutions are 3 and 8.

check.hint: You need two numbers that multiply to 24 and add to −11. Both must be negative.
check.explain:
Two numbers with product 24 and sum −11: −3 and −8.

(x − 3)(x − 8) = 0, so x = 3 or x = 8.

The larger solution is 8. Check: 64 − 88 + 24 = 0.

If you got −3 or −8, the signs in your factors were flipped. Multiply them back out to check the middle term.

screens.title: Get Zero on One Side First
screens.html:
Many equations do not arrive with 0 on one side. Before you factor, move every term to one side so the other side is 0.

If an equation says x(x − 2) = 15, it is tempting to set x = 15 and x − 2 = 15. That is wrong: the product is 15, not 0, so the zero product property does not apply. Multiply out, subtract 15, then factor.

After you find the answers, always check them in the original equation.

steps: Multiply out the left side: x<sup>2</sup> − 2x = 15.
x = 5 or x = −3. Check x = 5: 5(5 − 2) = 5(3) = 15. Check x = −3: −3(−3 − 2) = −3(−5) = 15.

mistakes.why: You wrote x(x − 4) = 21 and set x − 4 = 21. The product is 21, not 0, so that does not work. Subtract 21 first: x<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 21 = 0.
Check the signs in your factors. (x + 7)(x − 3) gives +4x. The correct factoring is (x − 7)(x + 3), so the positive solution is 7.
You cannot set x equal to 21. The right side must be 0 before you use the zero product property: x<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 21 = 0.

check.hint: Subtract 21 from both sides so the equation equals 0. Then factor.
check.explain:
Subtract 21: x2 − 4x − 21 = 0.

Product −21, sum −4: −7 and 3. (x − 7)(x + 3) = 0.

x = 7 or x = −3. The positive solution is 7.

Check: 72 − 4(7) = 49 − 28 = 21.

Setting x − 4 = 21 (to get 25) is the most common mistake: the zero product property needs 0 on one side.

screens.title: Common Factors and the Solution x = 0
screens.html:
When an equation has an x2 term and an x term but no number term, every term shares a factor of x. Factor out the greatest common factor (GCF).

Never divide both sides by x. Dividing by x assumes x is not 0, so it throws away the solution x = 0. Factor out x instead.

The same idea helps with any common factor. If every term is even, factor out 2 first; the numbers get smaller and easier.

why: You divided both sides by x (or by 4x), which loses the solution x = 0. Factor instead: 4x<sup>2</sup> − 28x = 0 becomes 4x(x − 7) = 0, so x = 0 or x = 7.
You made a sign slip in the last step. The factor x − 7 = 0 gives x = +7. Check: 4(−7)<sup>2</sup> = 196, but 28(−7) = −196.
You divided 4 by 28 instead of 28 by 4. From 4x(x − 7) = 0, the second solution is x = 7. Check: 4(7)<sup>2</sup> = 196 and 28(7) = 196.
check.hint: Move 28x to the left side, then factor out 4x. Do not divide by x.
check.explain:
Subtract 28x: 4x2 − 28x = 0.

Factor out 4x: 4x(x − 7) = 0.

4x = 0 gives x = 0; x − 7 = 0 gives x = 7.

The solutions are x = 0 and x = 7.

The most tempting wrong answer, x = 7 only, comes from dividing both sides by x. That step quietly assumes x is not 0, so it loses a real solution.

screens.title: Solving by Square Roots
screens.html:
If the equation has an x2 term but no x term, you do not need to factor. Get x2 (or the squared quantity) alone, then take the square root of both sides.

A positive number has two square roots. Always write ±: if x2 = 49, then x = 7 or x = −7.

This also works when a whole quantity is squared, like (x + 3)2 = 25. Take ± the square root, then solve two small equations.

If x2 equals a negative number, there is no real solution, because no real number squared is negative.

steps: First equation: divide by 2, x<sup>2</sup> = 49, so x = 7 or x = −7.
Second equation: take ± the square root, x + 3 = 5 or x + 3 = −5.
Subtract 3: x = 2 or x = −8. Check x = −8: (−8 + 3)<sup>2</sup> = (−5)<sup>2</sup> = 25.

mistakes.why: You added 1 instead of subtracting it. From x + 1 = −7, subtract 1: x = −8.
x + 1 = −7, so you still need to subtract 1 from both sides: x = −8.
x = 6 is the positive solution, from x + 1 = 7. The negative one comes from x + 1 = −7.

check.hint: Take ± the square root of both sides: x + 1 = 7 or x + 1 = −7. Then subtract 1.
check.explain:
Take ± the square root: x + 1 = 7 or x + 1 = −7.

Subtract 1: x = 6 or x = −8.

The negative solution is −8. Check: (−8 + 1)2 = (−7)2 = 49.

Stopping at −7 is the most common slip: that is the value of x + 1, not of x.

screens.title: The Quadratic Formula: Set It Up
screens.html:
Some quadratics cannot be factored with whole numbers. The quadratic formula solves every quadratic equation, and it is printed on the GED formula sheet:

x = (−b ± √(b2 − 4ac)) / (2a)

Start by writing the equation in standard form and labeling a, b, and c with their signs. Then find the part under the square root, b2 − 4ac. It is called the discriminant.

  • Put negative numbers in parentheses: if b = −4, then b2 = (−4)2 = 16.
  • If c is negative, −4ac becomes positive.

The discriminant tells you how many solutions to expect: positive means two, zero means one, negative means none.

example.prompt: For x<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 3 = 0, name a, b, and c and find the discriminant.
example.answer: The discriminant is 28, which is positive, so there are two solutions.

mistakes.why: You subtracted 40 instead of adding it. Here c = −5, so 4ac = 4(2)(−5) = −40, and 9 − (−40) = 49.
You squared −3 as −9. A negative times a negative is positive: (−3)<sup>2</sup> = 9. Then 9 + 40 = 49.

check.hint: Label a = 2, b = −3, c = −5. Put negatives in parentheses.
check.explain:
a = 2, b = −3, c = −5.

b2 = (−3)2 = 9.

4ac = 4(2)(−5) = −40.

b2 − 4ac = 9 − (−40) = 9 + 40 = 49.

If you got −31, you lost the negative sign on c.

screens.title: The Quadratic Formula: Finish It
screens.html:
Once you have the discriminant, the rest is three short steps:

  1. Take the square root of the discriminant.
  2. Write the top as −b + (root) for one answer and −b − (root) for the other.
  3. Divide the whole top by 2a.

−b means "the opposite of b." If b is negative, −b is positive. And the bottom is 2a, not a.

check.prompt: Use the quadratic formula to solve 3x2 + 5x − 2 = 0. What is the negative solution?

mistakes.why: You used +5 for −b. Since b = 5, −b = −5: x = (−5 ± 7)/6, which gives 1/3 and −2.
You divided by a (3) instead of 2a (6): (−5 − 7)/3 = −4. The bottom of the formula is 2a = 6.
You forgot to divide by 2a. (−5 − 7) = −12 is only the top; divide by 2(3) = 6 to get −2.

check.hint: a = 3, b = 5, c = −2. The discriminant is a perfect square.
check.explain:
a = 3, b = 5, c = −2.

b2 − 4ac = 25 − 4(3)(−2) = 25 + 24 = 49, and √49 = 7.

x = (−5 ± 7) / 6.

Plus: 2/6 = 1/3. Minus: −12/6 = −2.

The negative solution is −2. Check: 3(4) + 5(−2) − 2 = 12 − 10 − 2 = 0.

If you got −4, you divided by a instead of 2a.

screens.title: Rounded Answers with a Calculator
screens.html:
When the discriminant is not a perfect square, the answers are not whole numbers. On the GED you will usually round, often to the nearest tenth or hundredth.

  1. Find √(discriminant) on the calculator and write it to four decimal places.
  2. Compute −b + root and −b − root.
  3. Divide each by 2a.
  4. Round only at the end.

On the TI-30XS, enter the square root first and write it down. Typing the whole formula on one line is where parentheses get lost.

example.prompt: Solve x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 4 = 0. Round to the nearest hundredth.

check.prompt: Solve x2 + 2x − 7 = 0. What is the positive solution, rounded to the nearest hundredth?

mistakes.why: You used +2 for −b. Since b = 2, −b = −2: x = (−2 + 5.6569)/2 ≈ 1.83.
You divided only the square root by 2: −2 + 5.6569/2 ≈ 0.83. Divide the whole top: (−2 + 5.6569)/2 ≈ 1.83.
You forgot to divide by 2a = 2. The top, −2 + 5.6569 ≈ 3.66, must be divided by 2.

check.hint: a = 1, b = 2, c = −7. The discriminant is 4 + 28 = 32.
check.explain:
a = 1, b = 2, c = −7.

b2 − 4ac = 4 − 4(1)(−7) = 4 + 28 = 32. √32 ≈ 5.6569.

x = (−2 + 5.6569)/2 ≈ 1.8284 or x = (−2 − 5.6569)/2 ≈ −3.8284.

The positive solution is x ≈ 1.83.

If you got 0.83, you divided only the square root by 2 instead of the whole numerator.

screens.title: Choosing a Method
screens.html:
You now have three tools. Choosing the fastest one saves time on the test.

If the equation…UseExample
has no x termSquare roots5x2 = 80
factors with whole numbers you can find quicklyFactoringx2 + 5x + 6 = 0
has no constant termFactor out xx2 − 6x = 0
does not factor nicelyQuadratic formulax2 + 3x − 5 = 0

The quadratic formula works on every quadratic, so if you cannot find the factors in about 20 seconds, switch to the formula.

check.prompt: Which equation cannot be factored with whole numbers, so the quadratic formula is the best method?
why: This one factors: 2 × 3 = 6 and 2 + 3 = 5, so (x + 2)(x + 3) = 0 and x = −2 or x = −3.
This is a difference of two squares: (x + 7)(x − 7) = 0. Even faster, x<sup>2</sup> = 49 gives x = ±7 by square roots.
Every term has a factor of x: x(x − 6) = 0, so x = 0 or x = 6. No formula needed.
check.hint: For each equation, look for two whole numbers that multiply to c and add to b.
check.explain:
For x2 + 3x − 5 = 0, you need two whole numbers that multiply to −5 and add to 3. The only pairs for −5 are 1 and −5 (sum −4) and −1 and 5 (sum 4). Neither adds to 3, so it does not factor.

Use the formula: x = (−3 ± √29)/2. x2 + 3x − 5 = 0 is the answer.

The other three factor quickly: (x + 2)(x + 3), (x + 7)(x − 7), and x(x − 6).

screens.title: Parabolas: Shape and Direction
screens.html:
The graph of a quadratic function, y = ax2 + bx + c, is a U-shaped curve called a parabola.

  • If a is positive, the parabola opens up. Its turning point is the lowest point, a minimum.
  • If a is negative, it opens down. Its turning point is the highest point, a maximum.
  • The turning point is the vertex. The vertical line through it is the axis of symmetry; the two sides of the parabola are mirror images.

The graph shows y = x2 − 2x − 3, which opens up (a = 1), and y = −x2 + 2x + 3, which opens down (a = −1). Both turn at x = 1.

check.prompt:
Complete the statement about y = −2x2 + 8x − 3.

The parabola opens {{0}}, so its vertex is a {{1}}.

why: A parabola opens up when a is positive. Here a = −2 is negative, so it opens down.
A graph of y = ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + c always opens up or down, never sideways. Look at the sign of a = −2.
A minimum is the lowest point of a parabola that opens up. This one opens down, so its vertex is the highest point.
The y-intercept is where the graph crosses the y-axis, (0, −3). The vertex is the turning point, which here is a maximum.

check.hint: Look only at the sign of a, the number in front of x<sup>2</sup>.
check.explain:
a = −2 is negative, so the parabola opens down.

A parabola that opens down has a highest point, so its vertex is a maximum.

The 8 and the −3 do not affect the direction; only the sign of a does.

screens.title: Finding the Vertex
screens.html:
The x-coordinate of the vertex is

x = −b / (2a)

Substitute that x-value into the equation to find the y-coordinate. This formula is not on the formula sheet, so memorize it. (It is the front part of the quadratic formula.)

The y-coordinate of the vertex is the minimum value of y (if a > 0) or the maximum value (if a < 0).

example.prompt: Find the vertex of y = x<sup>2</sup> − 6x + 5.
steps: The vertex is (3, −4). Since a > 0, the minimum value is −4. The axis of symmetry is x = 3.

check.prompt: What is the y-coordinate of the vertex of y = 2x2 − 12x + 7?

mistakes.why: 3 is the x-coordinate of the vertex. Substitute x = 3 into the equation to get y: 2(9) − 36 + 7 = −11.
You used x = −3. Since b = −12, −b = 12, so x = 12/(2 × 2) = 3, not −3.
7 is the y-intercept (where x = 0), not the vertex. Find x = −b/(2a) = 3 first, then substitute.

check.hint: First find x = −b/(2a). Then substitute that x into the equation.
check.explain:
a = 2, b = −12. x = −(−12)/(2 × 2) = 12/4 = 3.

y = 2(3)2 − 12(3) + 7 = 18 − 36 + 7 = −11.

The vertex is (3, −11), so the y-coordinate is −11.

If you answered 3, you stopped after finding the x-coordinate.

screens.title: Intercepts: Where the Graph Crosses the Axes
screens.html:
• The y-intercept is where x = 0. For y = ax2 + bx + c it is always (0, c).
  • The x-intercepts are where y = 0. Find them by solving ax2 + bx + c = 0. They are written (x, 0).

So solving a quadratic equation and finding the x-intercepts of its graph are the same job. A parabola can cross the x-axis twice, touch it once (at the vertex), or miss it entirely.

The x-intercepts are the same distance from the axis of symmetry, which gives a quick check.

example.prompt: The graph shows y = −x<sup>2</sup> + 4x + 5. Find its intercepts and vertex.
steps: x-intercepts: −x<sup>2</sup> + 4x + 5 = 0. Multiply by −1: x<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 5 = 0, so (x − 5)(x + 1) = 0. Points (5, 0) and (−1, 0).
Vertex: x = −4/(2 × −1) = 2, y = −4 + 8 + 5 = 9. Vertex (2, 9). Check: 2 is halfway between −1 and 5.

check.prompt: The graph of y = x2 + 2x − 8 crosses the x-axis twice. Click the x-intercept that is to the right of the y-axis.
check.why: The most common wrong clicks are (4, 0), from flipping the signs in (x + 4)(x − 2), and (0, −8), which is the y-intercept. An x-intercept always sits on the x-axis, where y = 0.
check.hint: Set y = 0 and factor x<sup>2</sup> + 2x − 8. You need two numbers that multiply to −8 and add to 2.
check.explain:
Set y = 0: x2 + 2x − 8 = 0.

Product −8, sum 2: 4 and −2. (x + 4)(x − 2) = 0, so x = −4 or x = 2.

The x-intercepts are (−4, 0) and (2, 0). The one to the right of the y-axis is (2, 0).

Clicking (4, 0) is a sign error: the factor x + 4 gives x = −4.

screens.title: Maximum and Minimum in Word Problems
screens.html:
Many GED word problems describe something that rises and falls, like a ball, a rocket, or a company's profit. The question's words tell you which feature to find:

The question asks…Find
greatest, highest, maximum, best pricethe vertex (use its y-value for "how high" and its x-value for "when")
hits the ground, lands, breaks eventhe x-intercepts: set the expression = 0
starting height, value at time 0the y-intercept: c

In h = −16t2 + …, the −16 means the parabola opens down, so the vertex is a maximum.

example.prompt: An arrow is shot upward. Its height in feet after t seconds is h = −16t<sup>2</sup> + 80t. What is its greatest height?
steps: Greatest height is at the vertex: t = −80/(2 × −16) = −80/−32 = 2.5 seconds.
example.answer: The greatest height is 100 feet, reached after 2.5 seconds.

check.prompt: A ball is thrown upward from a balcony. Its height in feet after t seconds is h = −16t2 + 32t + 48. What is the ball's greatest height, in feet?

mistakes.why: 48 feet is the starting height (the value of h when t = 0). The ball keeps rising after it is thrown, so its greatest height is at the vertex.
1 is the time of the greatest height, t = −32/(2 × −16) = 1 second. Substitute it to find the height: −16 + 32 + 48 = 64.
3 seconds is when the ball lands (h = 0). The question asks for the greatest height, which is at the vertex.

check.hint: Find the time of the vertex with t = −b/(2a), then substitute it into the equation.
check.explain:
The greatest height is at the vertex: t = −32/(2 × −16) = −32/−32 = 1 second.

h = −16(1)2 + 32(1) + 48 = −16 + 32 + 48 = 64.

The greatest height is 64 feet.

If you answered 1, that is the time, not the height.

screens.title: Area Word Problems
screens.html:
Area problems often lead to quadratics. A typical one says the length is some amount more than the width.

  1. Let w be the width. Write the length in terms of w.
  2. Write area = length × width as an equation.
  3. Multiply out, get 0 on one side, and solve.
  4. Reject negative answers: a length cannot be negative.
  5. Answer the question that was asked (width or length?).

example.prompt: The length of a rectangular garden is 3 feet more than its width. The area is 70 square feet. Find the width.
steps: Width w, length w + 3. Area: w(w + 3) = 70.
example.answer: The width is 7 feet (the length is 10 feet).

check.prompt: The length of a rectangular rug is 4 feet more than its width. The rug's area is 60 square feet. What is the width of the rug, in feet?

mistakes.why: 10 feet is the length. The question asks for the width, which is 4 feet less: 6 feet.
That is √60, the side of a square with area 60. This rug is not a square; set up w(w + 4) = 60.
w = −10 is a solution of the equation, but a width cannot be negative. Use w = 6.

check.hint: Let w be the width, so the length is w + 4. Solve w(w + 4) = 60.
check.explain:
Width w, length w + 4. Area: w(w + 4) = 60.

w2 + 4w − 60 = 0. Product −60, sum 4: 10 and −6.

(w + 10)(w − 6) = 0, so w = −10 or w = 6.

A width cannot be negative, so the width is 6 feet (the length is 10 feet). Check: 6 × 10 = 60.

screens.title: Linear or Quadratic?
screens.html:
To decide from a table, look at how the outputs change when x goes up by 1.

x01234
Linear: y = 3x + 11471013
Quadratic: y = x2014916
  • First differences (subtract each output from the next): linear 3, 3, 3, 3; quadratic 1, 3, 5, 7.
  • If the first differences are all equal, the function is linear (a straight line).
  • If they are not equal, take the differences again. If these second differences are all equal (here 2, 2, 2), the function is quadratic (a parabola).

"Increasing" is not enough to make a function linear. The change must be the same every step.

check.prompt:
A function has these values.

x01234
y25101726

The first differences are {{0}}, so the function is {{1}}.

why: Only the first change is 3. Subtract each pair: 5 − 2 = 3, 10 − 5 = 5, 17 − 10 = 7, 26 − 17 = 9.
2 is the size of the second differences (5 − 3, 7 − 5, 9 − 7). The first differences are 3, 5, 7, 9.
A linear function changes by the same amount every step. These changes (3, 5, 7, 9) are different, so it is not linear.
The first differences are not equal, but the second differences are all 2. Constant second differences mean the function is quadratic.

check.hint: Subtract each y-value from the next one. Then check whether those changes are equal or grow steadily.
check.explain:
First differences: 5 − 2 = 3, 10 − 5 = 5, 17 − 10 = 7, 26 − 17 = 9. They are 3, 5, 7, 9.

Second differences: 2, 2, 2, which are constant, so the function is quadratic. (The rule is y = x2 + 2x + 2.)

screens.title: Comparing Functions
screens.html:
GED questions often give two functions in different forms (an equation, a table, a graph, or words) and ask which is greater, or which grows faster over an interval.

  • Which is greater at x = 5? Substitute 5 into both and compare.
  • Which increases more from x = 2 to x = 4? Find each function's change: f(4) − f(2) and g(4) − g(2).
  • A line changes by the same amount over every interval of the same width. An upward parabola changes faster and faster, so it eventually passes any line, even one that starts higher.

Do not judge from the first few values. Compute at the x-value the question asks about.

example.prompt: f(x) = 5x + 2 and g(x) = x<sup>2</sup>. Which is greater at x = 3? At x = 6?
steps: x = 3: f(3) = 17 and g(3) = 9, so f is greater.
x = 6: f(6) = 32 and g(6) = 36, so g is greater.
example.answer: f is greater at x = 3, but g is greater at x = 6. The parabola passes the line between x = 5 and x = 6.

check.prompt: f(x) = 4x + 5 and g(x) = x2 − 1. How much greater is g(6) than f(6)?

mistakes.why: You subtracted in the wrong order (f(6) − g(6) = 29 − 35). The question asks how much greater g(6) is: 35 − 29 = 6.
You treated x<sup>2</sup> as 2x, so g(6) became 11. Squaring means 6 × 6 = 36, so g(6) = 35 and 35 − 29 = 6.

check.hint: Find f(6) and g(6) separately. Then subtract f(6) from g(6).
check.explain:
f(6) = 4(6) + 5 = 24 + 5 = 29.

g(6) = 62 − 1 = 36 − 1 = 35.

g(6) − f(6) = 35 − 29 = 6.

If you got −6, you subtracted in the wrong order.

screens.title: Full Math Review: The GED Map
screens.html:
You have now studied every topic on the GED Mathematical Reasoning test. Here is how it fits together.

Part of the testSkills (course weeks)
Quantitative, about 45%Number sense (1); ratios, percents, interest (2); exponents, roots, scientific notation (3); data and probability (4); geometry (5–6)
Algebraic, about 55%Expressions and factoring (7); equations, inequalities, systems (8); lines and functions (9); quadratics (10)

The formula sheet gives you: area, perimeter, volume and surface area formulas; mean and median; slope and line equations; the standard form of a quadratic and the quadratic formula; the Pythagorean theorem; simple interest, distance, and total cost.

You must memorize: the vertex formula x = −b/(2a), percent change, mode and range, probability, exponent rules, and factoring patterns.

check.prompt: Which of these is not on the GED formula sheet, so you must memorize it?
why: The quadratic formula is printed on the formula sheet, along with the standard form ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + c = 0. The vertex formula is not.
The Pythagorean theorem, a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> = c<sup>2</sup>, is printed on the formula sheet. The vertex formula is not.
The slope formula, along with slope-intercept and point-slope form, is printed on the formula sheet. The vertex formula is not.
check.hint: Think about which parabola formula this lesson told you to memorize.
check.explain:
The formula sheet includes the quadratic formula, the Pythagorean theorem, and the slope formula. It does not include the vertex formula, x = −b/(2a), so you must know it from memory.

A memory aid: the vertex formula is the front part of the quadratic formula, −b over 2a, without the ± square root.

screens.title: Summary
screens.html:
• Standard form: ax2 + bx + c = 0. Signs belong to the numbers. Expect two solutions.
  • Factoring: get 0 on one side, factor, set each factor = 0, solve, check. Never divide by x.
  • No x term: isolate x2 and take ± the square root.
  • Quadratic formula (on the formula sheet): x = (−b ± √(b2 − 4ac)) / (2a). Find the discriminant first; divide the whole top by 2a.
  • Parabola: a > 0 opens up (minimum); a < 0 opens down (maximum). Vertex: x = −b/(2a), then substitute. y-intercept (0, c). x-intercepts: the solutions, (x, 0).
  • Word problems: "greatest" means the vertex; "lands" means set the expression = 0; reject negative lengths and times.
  • Linear: equal first differences. Quadratic: equal second differences. Compare functions by computing.
  • Review: know which formulas are on the sheet and which you must memorize.

Next: Practice Set A, which mixes quadratics with review from the whole course. If you score under 80%, practice the same skills again with Set B. Then take the Exit Check.

items.prompt:
What are the solutions of the equation below?

(x − 3)(x + 8) = 0
why: You copied the numbers from inside the factors. Solve each one: x − 3 = 0 gives x = 3, and x + 8 = 0 gives x = −8.
You solved x − 3 = 0 correctly but dropped the sign on the other factor. x + 8 = 0 gives x = −8, not 8.
You solved x + 8 = 0 correctly but flipped the other factor. x − 3 = 0 gives x = +3.
items.hint: Set each factor equal to 0 and solve each small equation.
items.explain:
By the zero product property, one of the factors must equal 0.

x − 3 = 0, so x = 3

x + 8 = 0, so x = −8

The solutions are x = 3 and x = −8. Check: (3 − 3)(3 + 8) = 0(11) = 0 and (−8 − 3)(−8 + 8) = (−11)(0) = 0.

The choice x = −3 and x = 8 comes from copying the numbers in the factors without solving. The solution always has the opposite sign of the number in the factor.

items.prompt: Solve 2x2 = 72. What is the positive solution?

mistakes.why: 36 is x<sup>2</sup>, not x. Take the square root of 36 to finish: x = 6.
You took the square root of 72 before dividing by 2. Divide first so x<sup>2</sup> is alone: x<sup>2</sup> = 36, then x = 6.

items.hint: Divide both sides by 2 to get x<sup>2</sup> alone. Then take the square root.
items.explain:
Divide both sides by 2: x2 = 36.

Take ± the square root: x = 6 or x = −6.

The positive solution is 6. Check: 2(6)2 = 2(36) = 72.

Stopping at 36 is the most common slip: that is the value of x2.

items.prompt: A jacket regularly priced at $64 is on sale for 25% off. What is the sale price?
why: $16 is the discount (25% of $64), not the sale price. Subtract it from the regular price: $64 − $16 = $48.
You subtracted 25 dollars instead of 25 percent. 25% of $64 is 0.25 × 64 = $16, so the sale price is $48.
You added 25% instead of taking it off: 64 × 1.25 = 80. A sale price is lower than the regular price.
items.hint: Find 25% of $64, then subtract it from $64. Or multiply $64 by 0.75.
items.explain:
Discount: 0.25 × 64 = $16.

Sale price: $64 − $16 = $48.

Shortcut: 25% off means you pay 75%, and 0.75 × 64 = 48.

The tempting wrong answer, $16, is the amount saved, not the price paid.

items.prompt: A circular rug has an area of 50.24 square feet. Using 3.14 for π, what is the radius of the rug, in feet?

mistakes.why: 16 is r<sup>2</sup>, not r. Take the square root of 16 to find the radius: r = 4.
You divided 16 by 2 instead of taking its square root. The square root of 16 is 4, because 4 × 4 = 16.

items.hint: Use A = πr<sup>2</sup>. Divide by 3.14 to get r<sup>2</sup> alone, then take the square root.
items.explain:
Area of a circle: A = πr2

50.24 = 3.14 × r2

Divide both sides by 3.14: r2 = 50.24 ÷ 3.14 = 16

Take the square root: r = 4 (a radius cannot be negative, so −4 is rejected)

The radius is 4 feet. A common mistake is to stop at 16, which is r2, not r.

items.prompt:
A student solves the equation x2 − 2x − 24 = 0 by factoring. Choose the correct option for each step.

Step 1 (factor): {{0}} = 0

Step 2 (solve): {{1}}

why: (x + 6)(x − 4) multiplies to x<sup>2</sup> + 2x − 24. The middle term has the wrong sign; switch the signs to get −2x.
(x − 8)(x + 3) multiplies to x<sup>2</sup> − 5x − 24. The product is right, but the sum is −5, not −2.
(x − 12)(x + 2) multiplies to x<sup>2</sup> − 10x − 24. The product is right, but the sum is −10, not −2.
You copied the numbers from the factors without solving. x − 6 = 0 gives x = 6, and x + 4 = 0 gives x = −4.
You dropped the negative sign. x + 4 = 0 gives x = −4, not 4.
You used numbers from the original equation instead of the factors. Solve x − 6 = 0 and x + 4 = 0.

items.hint: You need two numbers that multiply to −24 and add to −2.
items.explain:
Step 1: Two numbers with a product of −24 and a sum of −2 are −6 and 4, so the expression factors as (x − 6)(x + 4).

Check by multiplying: x2 + 4x − 6x − 24 = x2 − 2x − 24.

(x + 6)(x − 4) = x2 + 2x − 24 has the wrong middle sign. (x − 8)(x + 3) = x2 − 5x − 24 and (x − 12)(x + 2) = x2 − 10x − 24 have the wrong middle term.

Step 2: x − 6 = 0 gives x = 6; x + 4 = 0 gives x = −4. So x = 6 or x = −4.

Check x = −4: 16 + 8 − 24 = 0.

items.prompt: The equation 5x2 = 30x has two solutions. One of them is 0. What is the other solution?

mistakes.why: Check the sign. 5x(x − 6) = 0 gives x − 6 = 0, so x = +6. Check: 5(36) = 180 and 30(6) = 180.
You divided 5 by 30 instead of 30 by 5. From 5x<sup>2</sup> = 30x, the nonzero solution is x = 30/5 = 6.
You multiplied 30 by 5. Factor instead: 5x<sup>2</sup> − 30x = 5x(x − 6), so x − 6 = 0 and x = 6.

items.hint: Subtract 30x from both sides, then factor out 5x.
items.explain:
Subtract 30x: 5x2 − 30x = 0.

Factor out 5x: 5x(x − 6) = 0.

5x = 0 gives x = 0; x − 6 = 0 gives x = 6.

The other solution is 6. Check: 5(6)2 = 180 and 30(6) = 180.

Dividing both sides by x also gives 6 here, but it would hide the solution x = 0, which is why factoring is the safe habit.

items.prompt: The graph of y = x2 + 2x − 15 crosses the x-axis at two points. What is the x-coordinate of the point that is farther to the right?

mistakes.why: You flipped the signs in the factors. x<sup>2</sup> + 2x − 15 = (x + 5)(x − 3), so the x-intercepts are x = −5 and x = 3.
−15 is the y-intercept value (where x = 0). The x-intercepts are where y = 0: solve x<sup>2</sup> + 2x − 15 = 0.
x = −5 is the x-intercept on the left. The one farther right is x = 3.

items.hint: x-intercepts are where y = 0. Set x<sup>2</sup> + 2x − 15 = 0 and factor.
items.explain:
Set y = 0: x2 + 2x − 15 = 0.

Product −15, sum 2: 5 and −3. (x + 5)(x − 3) = 0.

x = −5 or x = 3. The intercepts are (−5, 0) and (3, 0).

The one farther right has x-coordinate 3.

An answer of 5 comes from copying the number from the factor x + 5 instead of solving it.

items.prompt: The graph of y = −x2 − 4x + 1 is a parabola. Click the point on the grid that is its vertex.
items.why: The most common wrong click is a point at x = 2, from losing a sign in −b/(2a). Here a = −1 and b = −4, so −b = 4 and 2a = −2, giving x = 4/(−2) = −2.
items.hint: a = −1 and b = −4. Find x = −b/(2a) carefully, then substitute it to find y.
items.explain:
a = −1 and b = −4.

x = −b/(2a) = −(−4)/(2 × −1) = 4/(−2) = −2.

y = −(−2)2 − 4(−2) + 1 = −4 + 8 + 1 = 5.

The vertex is (−2, 5). Because a is negative, it is the highest point of the parabola.

Watch the first term: −(−2)2 means square first, then take the opposite, so it is −4, not +4.

items.prompt:
A worker recorded the number of customers she served on each of six days:

12, 15, 15, 18, 20, 28

Which statements about the data are true? Select two answers.
why: 20 appears only once. The mode is the value that appears most often, and 15 appears twice.
You subtracted 15 from 28. The range uses the least value: 28 − 12 = 16.
You used only one of the two middle values. With six values, the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th: (15 + 18) ÷ 2 = 16.5.
You divided the sum, 108, by 5 instead of 6. There are six days of data, so the mean is 108 ÷ 6 = 18.
items.hint: Mean = sum ÷ number of values. With an even number of values, the median is the average of the two middle values.
items.explain:
Mean: 12 + 15 + 15 + 18 + 20 + 28 = 108, and 108 ÷ 6 = 18. True.

Median: the two middle values are 15 and 18, so the median is (15 + 18) ÷ 2 = 16.5. True.

Mode: 15 appears twice, so the mode is 15, not 20.

Range: 28 − 12 = 16, not 13.

A median of 15 comes from using only one middle value. A mean of 21.6 comes from dividing 108 by 5 instead of 6.

The true statements are the mean is 18 and the median is 16.5.

items.prompt: A line passes through the points (−2, 5) and (4, −7). Which equation represents the line?
why: You found the right slope but treated −2(−2) as −4, so 5 = −4 + b gave b = 9. A negative times a negative is positive: 5 = 4 + b, so b = 1.
You dropped the sign of the slope. The y-values fall from 5 to −7 while x rises, so the slope is −12/6 = −2, not 2.
You divided the change in x by the change in y (6/−12). Slope is rise over run: −12/6 = −2.
items.hint: Find the slope with (y<sub>2</sub> − y<sub>1</sub>)/(x<sub>2</sub> − x<sub>1</sub>). Then substitute one point into y = mx + b to find b.
items.explain:
Slope: m = (−7 − 5) / (4 − (−2)) = −12 / 6 = −2

Substitute the point (−2, 5) into y = −2x + b:

5 = −2(−2) + b

5 = 4 + b, so b = 1

The equation is y = −2x + 1. Check with (4, −7): −2(4) + 1 = −8 + 1 = −7.

y = −2x + 9 comes from treating −2(−2) as −4. y = −½x + 4 comes from dividing the x-change by the y-change.

items.prompt:
What are the solutions of the equation below, rounded to the nearest hundredth?

3x2 − 2x − 4 = 0
why: You used −2 for −b. Since b = −2, −b = +2, so the top is 2 ± 7.2111, not −2 ± 7.2111.
You divided by a (3) instead of 2a (6). The bottom of the formula is 2 × 3 = 6.
You computed 4ac as 24 instead of 48: 4(3)(−4) = −48, so the discriminant is 4 + 48 = 52, not 28.
items.hint: Use the quadratic formula with a = 3, b = −2, and c = −4. Remember that −b is positive 2.
items.explain:
a = 3, b = −2, c = −4

b2 − 4ac = (−2)2 − 4(3)(−4) = 4 + 48 = 52

√52 ≈ 7.2111

x = (−(−2) ± 7.2111) / (2 × 3) = (2 ± 7.2111) / 6

x ≈ 9.2111 / 6 ≈ 1.535, which rounds to 1.54

x ≈ −5.2111 / 6 ≈ −0.869, which rounds to −0.87

The solutions are x ≈ 1.54 and x ≈ −0.87.

0.87 and −1.54 come from using −2 instead of +2 for −b. 3.07 and −1.74 come from dividing by a (3) instead of 2a (6). 1.22 and −0.55 come from computing 4ac as 24 instead of 48.

items.prompt: A rectangular patio has an area of 112 square feet. Its length is 2 feet less than twice its width. What is the width of the patio, in feet?

mistakes.why: 14 feet is the length (2 × 8 − 2). The question asks for the width.
That is √112, the side of a square with area 112. This patio is not a square; set up w(2w − 2) = 112.
w = −7 solves the equation, but a width cannot be negative. Use the positive solution, 8.

items.hint: Let w be the width, so the length is 2w − 2. Area = length × width. Divide the equation by 2 before factoring.
items.explain:
Width w, length 2w − 2. Area: w(2w − 2) = 112.

Multiply out: 2w2 − 2w = 112, so 2w2 − 2w − 112 = 0.

Divide every term by 2: w2 − w − 56 = 0.

Product −56, sum −1: −8 and 7. (w − 8)(w + 7) = 0, so w = 8 or w = −7.

A width cannot be negative, so the width is 8 feet. Check: the length is 2(8) − 2 = 14, and 8 × 14 = 112.

If you answered 14, you found the length instead of the width.

items.prompt:
A ball is thrown upward from the roof of a building 192 feet tall. Its height h, in feet, after t seconds is

h = −16t2 + 64t + 192

How many seconds after it is thrown does the ball hit the ground?

mistakes.why: 2 seconds is when the ball is highest, t = −64/(2 × −16). It hits the ground when h = 0.
t = −2 solves the equation, but time after the throw cannot be negative. Use t = 6.
256 feet is the greatest height, not a time. The question asks when h = 0.

items.hint: The ball hits the ground when h = 0. Divide every term by −16 before factoring.
items.explain:
The ball hits the ground when h = 0: −16t2 + 64t + 192 = 0.

Divide every term by −16: t2 − 4t − 12 = 0.

Product −12, sum −4: −6 and 2. (t − 6)(t + 2) = 0, so t = 6 or t = −2.

Time cannot be negative, so the ball lands after 6 seconds.

Check: −16(36) + 64(6) + 192 = −576 + 384 + 192 = 0.

The most tempting wrong answer is 2 seconds, which is the time of the greatest height.

items.prompt:
A model rocket is launched from the ground. Its height h, in feet, after t seconds is

h = −16t2 + 96t

What is the rocket's greatest height, in feet?

You flipped the signs. −x<sup>2</sup> − 2x + 8 = 0 becomes x<sup>2</sup> + 2x − 8 = 0, which is (x + 4)(x − 2) = 0, so x = −4 or x = 2.
x-intercepts lie on the x-axis, so y = 0. Write them as (x, 0): (−4, 0) and (2, 0).

items.prompt: A theater models its weekly ticket revenue R, in dollars, when tickets cost p dollars: R = −5p2 + 200p. What is the greatest weekly revenue, in dollars?

mistakes.why: $20 is the ticket price that gives the greatest revenue. Substitute p = 20 to find the revenue: −2,000 + 4,000 = 2,000.
p = 40 is where the revenue drops to $0 (an intercept). The greatest revenue is at the vertex, halfway between 0 and 40.
You multiplied −5 by 20 instead of by 20<sup>2</sup>. −5(400) = −2,000, so R = −2,000 + 4,000 = 2,000.

items.explain:
Vertex: p = −200/(2 × −5) = −200/−10 = 20 dollars.

R = −5(20)2 + 200(20) = −2,000 + 4,000 = 2,000.

The greatest weekly revenue is $2,000.

If you answered 20, you found the best price, not the revenue.

items.prompt: A triangular sail has a base that is 4 feet longer than its height. The area of the sail is 30 square feet. What is the height of the sail?
why: 10 feet is the base, h + 4. The question asks for the height.
You left out the ½ in the triangle area formula: h(h + 4) = 30 gives about 3.8. A triangle's area is ½ × base × height.
7.7 feet is about √60. That would be the side of a square with area 60; this is a triangle whose base is 4 feet more than its height.
items.explain:
Height h, base h + 4. Area: ½ × h × (h + 4) = 30.

Multiply by 2: h(h + 4) = 60, so h2 + 4h − 60 = 0.

Product −60, sum 4: 10 and −6. (h + 10)(h − 6) = 0, so h = −10 or h = 6.

A height cannot be negative, so the height is 6 feet. Check: ½ × 6 × 10 = 30.

10 feet is the base, the most tempting wrong answer.

options: When x = 6, g(x) is greater than f(x).
When x = 4, g(x) is greater than f(x).
f and g have the same y-intercept.

x = 4: f(4) = 28 and g(4) = 24. f is greater, so that statement is false.

The parabola starts lower but passes the line between x = 4 and x = 5.

why: You added the width and height (24 + 18). The diagonal comes from the squares: √(576 + 324) = √900 = 30.

The width and height are the legs; the diagonal is the hypotenuse.

242 + 182 = 576 + 324 = 900, and √900 = 30.

items.prompt: A coffee shop sold 50 drinks for a total of $190. Small drinks cost $3 and large drinks cost $5. How many large drinks were sold?

mistakes.why: 30 is the number of small drinks. Large drinks: 50 − 30 = 20.
You divided $190 by $5 as if every drink were large. Use two equations: s + l = 50 and 3s + 5l = 190.

items.explain:
Let s = small drinks and l = large drinks.

s + l = 50 and 3s + 5l = 190.

Substitute s = 50 − l: 3(50 − l) + 5l = 190 → 150 + 2l = 190 → 2l = 40 → l = 20.

20 large drinks (and 30 small). Check: 30 × 3 + 20 × 5 = 90 + 100 = 190.

notes:
Week 10 Study Sheet: Quadratics and Final Review

Solving Quadratics

Standard form: ax2 + bx + c = 0 (signs go with the numbers)

  1. Factoring: get 0 on one side, factor, set each factor = 0. x2 − 5x − 14 = 0 → (x + 2)(x − 7) = 0 → x = −2, 7
  2. GCF: 3x2 = 12x → 3x(x − 4) = 0 → x = 0, 4. Never divide by x.
  3. Square roots (no x term): 3x2 = 75 → x2 = 25 → x = ±5
  4. Quadratic formula (on the formula sheet): x = (−b ± √(b2 − 4ac)) / (2a). Discriminant b2 − 4ac first; divide the whole top by 2a.

Parabolas: y = ax2 + bx + c

  • a > 0: opens up (minimum). a < 0: opens down (maximum).
  • Vertex: x = −b/(2a), then substitute for y. Not on the formula sheet.
  • Axis of symmetry: the vertical line through the vertex.
  • y-intercept: (0, c). x-intercepts: solve ax2 + bx + c = 0; points (x, 0).

Word problems: "greatest/highest/maximum" → vertex; "lands/hits the ground" → set = 0; reject negative times and lengths; answer what was asked.

Linear vs. Quadratic

LinearQuadratic
Equationy = mx + by = ax2 + bx + c
GraphStraight lineParabola
TableEqual first differences: 1, 4, 7, 10 (+3)Equal second differences: 0, 1, 4, 9 (+1, +3, +5 → +2)
ComparingSubstitute and compute; an upward parabola eventually passes any line.

Memorize (not on the formula sheet)

  • Vertex: x = −b/(2a)
  • Percent change = change ÷ original
  • Mode (most frequent); range = max − min
  • Probability = favorable ÷ total
  • Exponent rules and factoring patterns

On the formula sheet

  • Area, perimeter, circle formulas
  • Volume and surface area of solids
  • Mean and median
  • Slope, slope-intercept, point-slope
  • Quadratic formula, Pythagorean theorem
  • Simple interest, distance, total cost

Test day: 115 minutes, about 46 questions (about 2.5 min each). Part 1 (5 questions) has no calculator and you cannot return to it. Plug answer choices back in. Flag, guess, and move on. Never leave a blank.

Top mistakes: not setting the equation to 0; dividing by x; forgetting the negative root; sign errors with −b and b2; dividing only part of the top by 2a; mixing up x- and y-intercepts; giving the time when the question asks for the height.
